The center hole operation is used to provide starting holes for other drilling operations.
The drill operation is the primary hole making operation. It is used to drill basic holes.
The peck-drill operation is a deep drilling method. The drill withdraws to the approach plane after advancing a specified distance into the hole, facilitating chip removal.
With a chip-break operation, the drill withdraws a specified distance after advancing into the hole to prevent the binding of chips.
Use the bore operation to enlarge, finish and accurately locate holes.
With a fine bore operation, the boring bar enters the hole off-center, centers and bores from the bottom of the hole upward, avoiding drag marks along sides of the hole.
Use the ream operation for finishing by removing a small amount of material from a pre-drilled hole.
Use the tap operation to cut threads in a hole.
Use the counterbore operation to spot-face, making room for the heads of bolts or screws, or to enlarge holes.
Use the countersink operation to machine a cone shaped enlargement at the top of a hole.

The profile cut operation cuts any number of open or closed curve boundaries or CAM Components containing geometry profiles. This allows engraving operations or complex patterns to be machined without error.
The spiral cut operation is a facing (area clearance) or pocketing technique, which advances the tool at each depth by proceeding toward or away from the part boundaries.
The box cut operation is a facing (area clearance) or pocketing technique, similar to the zigzag cut except the cuts are all in the same direction. The tool is lifted between each cut.

The zigzag cut operation is a facing (area clearance) or pocketing technique. It advances the tool at each depth though a sequence of straight parallel cuts, reversing the tool direction at the end of each cut.
With the contour cut operation, a medial or spine curve is calculated for each cutting zone. Tool movement proceeds in cuts generated parallel or perpendicular to that curve.
The Chamfer Cut operation will accept profiles, curves, surfaces or chamfer features. The chamfer feature provides control for Offset, Draft, Depth, Chamfer Side and Spine Curves.
Use the Helical Cut operation to machine male and female threads.

Ramp Cut toolpaths start at Tool Home Start or pre-drill point. Starting from the top plane, the toolpath then ramps down evenly as determined by the Ramp Angle until it reaches the bottom plane. When the toolpath reaches the bottom plane, a line segment is created to reach Tool Home End.

The Corner Cut operation will accept curves, surfaces and edges as inputs. It does not currently do any further analysis of the surface shape, so it will not automatically extract radius if a fillet like surface is selected.
The topface cut operation machines all planar faces defined in surfaces or part.
The part nesting operation is used to arrange parts on a plate of material to maximize the number of parts that will fit.
Use the Thread Mill operation to machine male and female threads.
This is a 3 axis surface engraving operation (i.e., characters on parts). The input requirements for this operation are the surface part and the engraving characters.

The Inter Path Move operation is provided so that you can create safe moves when a tool moves between tool paths. The result will be either a 3 axis or 5 axis motion sequence from the end of the previous tool path to the start of the following tool path.
The map cut operation cuts any number of trimmed surfaces or solids. The cutting motion proceeds in a series of parallel cuts in one or both directions.

The side cut operation is a 2-1/2 axis tool motion controlled by depth of cut and surface or solid geometry. The tool can ramp from one depth down to the next and the cuts can be sorted based on cutting region or depth.

The iso cut operation uses the isolines (lines of constant U or V parameter value) of individual surfaces to guide the tool contact point. It can produce a very nice surface finish. However, it is NOT a gouge-free tool path.
The 3 axis spiral cut operation is an area clearance technique which cuts any number of trimmed surfaces or solids using any number of closed boundaries to enclose the cutting motion.
The 3 axis box cut operation is an area clearance technique, similar to 3-axis zigzag cut except the cuts are all in the same direction. The tool is lifted between each cut.

The 3 axis zigzag cut operation is an area clearance technique which cuts any number of trimmed surfaces or solids using any number of closed boundaries to enclose the cutting motion. The tool advances at each depth through a sequence of parallel cuts, reversing the tool direction at the end of each cut.
The 3 axis profile cut operation cuts any number of trimmed surfaces or solids using any number of open or closed curve boundaries to guide the tool centerline.
The spiral rough operation is used for the removal of rough stock explicitly defined by profile, surface or solid stock definitions.
The box rough operation is used for the removal of rough stock explicitly defined by profile, surface or solid stock definitions.
The zigzag rough operation is used for the removal of rough stock explicitly defined by profile, surface or solid stock definitions.
The spiral cast rough operation is used for the removal of implicitly defined stock using thickness values for remaining stock and offsets for stock removal.
The box cast rough operation is used for the removal of implicitly defined stock using thickness values for remaining stock and offsets for stock removal.
The zigzag cast rough operation is used for the removal of implicitly defined stock using thickness values for remaining stock and offsets for stock removal.
The rest cut operation removes material remaining after previous milling operations.

The pencil trace operation removes material in creases and tight curvature regions on the part. This is useful for both cleanup and from relieving material near steep surfaces in preparation for other milling operations.
The scallop removal operation is a 3 axis tool path that requires the input of either a map cut or a side cut reference operation.
With the 3 axis contour cut operation, a medial or spine curve is calculated for each cutting zone. Tool movement proceeds in cuts generated parallel or perpendicular to that curve.
The contour rough operation is used for the removal of rough stock explicitly defined by profile, surface or solid stock definitions.
The Contour Cast Rough Operation is used for the removal of implicitly defined stock using thickness values for remaining stock and offsets for stock removal.

The peeling cut operation combines 2-1/2 axis motion in steep areas on the part and 3-axis motion in less steep regions. This improves machining efficiency and surface finish. You have complete control over the cutting pattern for the 3 axis motion.
The lace cut operation is a parallel milling technique controlled by stepping parameters.
The z level cut (also referred to as side cut) is used to machine steep walls.

The drive curve cut operation is similar to the offset 3D cut that starts from a custom set of curves. The starting curves can be open or closed. In general it is used like the flowing cut for milling along features.
The high speed offset 2D cut operation is used for 2D area clearance.

Multiple CAM profile features can be defined for this operation. Each feature group is considered one span. The curve pick sequence when defining the profile feature is very important for this operation.
This is a more advanced version of the lace cut operation suited for high speed machining.
The offset 3D cut operation is used when a smooth and continuous tool path is required in the part.
The pencil cut operation is used to clear corners as a follow up to other QuickMilling operations.
The rough lace cut operation is a parallel milling technique controlled by stepping parameters. It is used for the removal of explicitly defined rough stock.
The rough offset 2D cut is used for 2D area clearance of explicitly defined rough stock.
The rough plunge cut operation is used to rough out large parts. These can include deep cores and cavities, high shoulder slots and straight or sloped walls.
The rough drill cut operation is used to create access holes to pocket features on the part to be machined.
The Flow 3D cut operation will "morph" a pattern between pairs of guiding curves. The Flow 3D Cut could follow a Bulge Cut in a tool path sequence.

This operation create a network of bulges on a surface using two intersecting curves referred to as a drive curve (Directrix) and a generator curve (Generatrix). This operation is useful in dispersion networks for automotive lighting parts or as an artistic hammer-paint effect.
This is a 2 axis surface engraving operation (i.e., characters on flat parts). After creating the text, use the Explode Text & Dimensions command to create the curves to select for the CAM features.

The cutter contact paths follow the constant U or constant V parameter lines of the part surfaces. This operation type can quickly provide efficient and smooth tool motion. The tool is usually well placed even on near-horizontal and near-vertical part shapes.

SmoothFlow is a HSM cycle that tries to keep the tool uniformly engaged in material and retract as few times as possible.  There are two flavors: a unidirectional (climb, conventional) version and a zigzag one.  The unidirectional version adds around 10% of overcutting.

SmoothFlow technology was introduced to machine cavities and pockets safely and efficiently by maintaining constant material removal during roughing thus extending tool life and reducing machine wear and tear.

The Angle Limiting Finishing cut operation is used when smooth and steep tool path are both required in the vicinity of steep walls, milling in uncut or uncutable places or when milling the entirely part as a whole.
The Corner Finish operation is used to clear corners as a follow up to other QuickMilling operations.
The Flat Finish operation is used to machine all planar faces defined in surfaces or part.

The 5 axis plane cut creates a cutting pattern based on parallel cuts at a user specified angle with respect to the frames X axis. This cutting pattern can be used to control the tool tip or the contact location of the tool on the part.
The tool axis is controlled by drive surfaces with which the side of the tool maintains contact. The bottom of the tool (contact point) is controlled by part surfaces.
The 5 axis Drive Curve Cut uses 3D driving curves to calculate the tool path. The cutter is driven along these curves and respects the surface geometry to be cut.
The interactive cut operation provides additional flexibility by allowing you to create a sequence of 5 axis swarf cut tool motions by specifying groups of part, check and drive surfaces.

The 5 axis Flow Cut operation requires either a 5 axis Swarfcut or a 5 axis Drive Curve Cut as a reference operation that contains two separated cuts. This operation is very useful for machining areas between two tilted walls (turbine blades for example).

The 5 axis Side Cut operation base upon different axis control options, it allows you to position the cutter in various orientations. This operation is a good choice for turbine top machining or complex pocket finishing with point control.

Each 5 axis Guide Surface Iso Cut operation must have drive surface(s) selected in its feature list with general surfaces input as the cutting target. The guide surface defined by a drive surface forces tool axis to follow its normals along the isolines.

The Area Mill operation uses selected faces as drive geometry. Specify part geometry and cut area, Edit containment method and region pattern to create toolpath. Recommanded for finishing specific areas.
